ihatemailto.title: I Hate Mailto
ihatemailto.description: I got tired of mailto: links opening an email client I never use, so I built I Hate Mailto, my first browser extension. It intercepts mailto:, tel: and sms: clicks and copies the details to your clipboard instead, with a clear toast confirming what happened. Toast colors, position and duration are customizable, and you can turn it off on specific sites. Built with WXT and TypeScript.
ihatemailto.story: A lightweight browser add-on that stops mailto:, tel: and sms: links from launching apps you don't want, and copies their details to your clipboard instead.

guessTheWord.title: Guess The Word
guessTheWord.description: A deliberately simple Skribbl.io clone I built in 2022 with a classmate. One player draws a word and everyone else tries to guess it. It's written in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS on top of Node.js and Socket.IO, which handles the real-time communication between players.
guessTheWord.story: A fun project I built with a classmate, and a great way to learn about real-time communication and game development.

phatris.title: Phatris
phatris.description: Phatris is a Tetris clone I built in 2022 with a classmate, with several game modes to choose from. It runs on the Phaser 3 framework, is played with the keyboard, and shows a scoreboard stored in a MongoDB database.
phatris.story: My first official school project, and where I learned the ropes of game development and Phaser 3.

bmpManipulator.title: Bitmap Manipulator
bmpManipulator.description: A Java command-line tool that reads bitmap images at the byte level, with no libraries involved. You can apply filters, change colors and edit individual pixels, or turn an image into ASCII art using custom characters.
bmpManipulator.story: Built while I was learning Java. It taught me a lot about the bitmap format and how to manipulate images byte by byte.

movieSurvey.title: Movie Survey
movieSurvey.description: Movie Survey is a React Native app that helps a group pick a movie democratically. Users vote on a selection of films, the app generates a ranking, and it can run new rounds of voting based on previous results. It uses WebSockets for real-time communication and MongoDB for data storage, and works on both Android and iOS.
movieSurvey.story: My Business IT exam project, where I showcased my skills in mobile app development and real-time communication.

databaseComparison.title: Database Comparison
databaseComparison.description: An analysis built around two equivalent web APIs: one backed by a relational database (MySQL), the other by a document database (MongoDB). Both support CRUD operations on a sample dataset, so I could compare the two in terms of execution speed and scalability.
databaseComparison.story: A project from my Business IT studies, where I put my skills in database design and management, API development and comparative analysis to work.

addictionRecovery.title: Clean Progress Tracker
addictionRecovery.description: A React Native mobile app that helps people track their progress in overcoming addictions. Users can create time counters, add notes, and reset them after a relapse. Data is handled by a MongoDB backend with an Express REST API, keeping user profiles and data private.
addictionRecovery.story: A project from my Business IT studies, where I showed what I can do in mobile app development and data management.

workoutTracker.title: WorkoutTracker
workoutTracker.description: A mobile workout-tracking app I built with two other students from my year, and my first time using React Native with Expo. Data is handled by a MongoDB backend with an Express REST API, which manages user profiles and data.
workoutTracker.story: My first dive into mobile app development, and where I learned React Native and Expo.
